messages:
pen-test-bot: Automated pen-test scan uploaded new findings (ptest-2026-03-17). Summary:
- Issue A: KMS alias enumeration via ListAliases on Private deployments (insufficient auth check in control plane proxy). PoC attached.
- Issue B: Missing audit log entries for key-rotation events in some Private clusters (audit exporter not emitting pre/post rotation entries).
Impact: information exposure + compliance gap for regulated customers. Recommended triage severity: P2. Evidence: s3://redwood-pen/poc/ptest-2026-03-17.zip

alice: Support flagged an escalation from ACME (CS-789). After we rotated keys they reported 500s + a billing spike. We need repro steps and a retest plan — possible relation to rotation/auth retries.

ben: Can someone paste repro steps and the exact logs they saw? We need to confirm whether alias enumeration is exploitable externally or requires auth.

carla: I ran a repro on private staging (acme-stg-1). Steps:
1) POST /v1/kms/rotate {"key_id":"alias/acme"} -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>'
2) observed 502 from hostpool for ~45s with repeated client retries
3) billing meter showed a burst because service clients retried on 502s
Logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T09:05:12Z auth: rotate request accepted for alias/acme by svc-account:infra
2026-03-17T09:05:12Z kms: starting key material swap
2026-03-17T09:06:00Z proxy: upstream 502
// NOTE: missing: audit.kms.rotate pre-rotation entry (audit exporter did not persist)
```
Gist with full logs: <redacted-gist-link>

dave: I've got a patch that forces the audit logger to flush pre-rotation and always emit post-rotation hooks. PR #4523. Can we get a staging deploy and run retests?

infra-bot: deploy: staging rollout completed at 2026-03-17T10:10Z (rev ab12c).

carla: Running staging retest now: 5 rotation attempts against alias/acme, all returned 200. Audit entries present for pre/post rotation. No 502s observed in 5 tries. Uploading artifacts. Still need to validate on Private with HSM-backed KMS.

eve: Quick note on severity: pen-test labeled P2 but compliance is pushing for P1 for any missing audit evidence when HSM/private deployments are involved. That has regulatory impact for PCI/ SOC2 customers. Thoughts?

ben: We should be specific: If audit export was enabled for the cluster and events are missing -> P1. If export was disabled and it's an ops misconfig -> P2 but urgent. For ACME, their cluster had export enabled per onboarding doc.

alice: Agreed. Reclassifying affected ACME finding to P1. Action items:
- dave: backport PR to 2025.12 private branch and patch acme-prod-1 cluster (ETA 4h).
- carla: run private retest and upload evidence to pen-test ticket.
- ben: investigate the billing spike root cause and produce mitigation (rate-limit client retries during rotation).
- eve: draft notice to compliance + ACME CISO.
I'll coordinate with support.

carla: Uploaded staging retest artifacts: s3://redwood-pen/ret/ptest-2026-03-17/staging-results.log
Scheduling private cluster test at 11:30 PT and will report back.

pen-test-bot: Re-run scheduled dynamic scan queued for 2026-03-17T11:45Z; will post results to the same thread.

dave: Backport applied, patch rolled to acme-prod-1 at 2026-03-17T11:20Z. Initiated rolling restart.

infra-bot: deploy: acme-prod-1 patch roll started (rev ab12c-b2), 5 nodes rolling, health-check threshold 95%.

carla: Private retest complete: 5/5 rotation attempts succeeded. Audit entries present for pre/post rotation on acme-prod-1. Billing spike not reproduced after patch; looks like retry flood was mitigated by the improved failure mode. Evidence uploaded: s3://redwood-pen/ret/ptest-2026-03-17/acme-prod-1-results.log

eve: Compliance requests a short report (one pager) listing impacted customers, timeline, and mitigation steps before we mark this as fully resolved. I'll draft and share.

alice: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident tracker: CS-789 -> security escalated -> severity=P1 (affected: ACME). Posting follow-up postmortem and timeline once eve's report is ready. Leaving thread open until compliance ack.

ben: :thumbsup:
